B544: Derived from income or expenditure share of the highest 20% and lowest 20% groups by income.
B545: HDI rank figures are not comparable across years.
B546: Refers to the expected number of years of schooling from primary to tertiary level of education.
B547: Refers to the average number of completed years of education among the population aged 25 years and older (excluding years spent repeating individual grades), by highest level of education attained.
B548: The UIS defines a qualified teacher as one who has at least the minimum academic qualifications required for teaching their subjects at the relevant level in a given economy in a given academic year.
B549: Refers to the economically active population aged 16 years and older who are capable of working, are participating in, or are willing to participate in, economic activities; and includes the employed and unemployed. The sum of employed and unemployed does not add up to total labor force because unemployed refers to urban areas only.
B550: Refers to persons engaged in social labor and receiving remuneration or earning business income.
B551: Refers to primary industry that includes agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery industries (except support services to agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery industries).
B552: Refers to secondary industry that includes mining (except auxiliary activities of mining); manufacturing (except repairing of metal products, machinery, and equipment); production and supply of electricity, steam, gas, and water; and construction.
B553: Refers to all other industries not included in primary and secondary industry.
B555: For 2000–2021, data refer to urban registered unemployment rate. For 2022 onward, data refer to year-end urban surveyed unemployment rate.
B556: Includes mining and quarrying; electricity, gas, steam, and air-conditioning supply; and water supply; sewerage, waste management, and remediation activities.
B557: For 2000 onward, data are combined with other service activities.
B558: Includes information and communication; professional, scientific, and technical activities; administrative and support service activities; public administration and defense; compulsory social security; education; human health and social work activities; arts, entertainment, and recreation; and activities of households as employers; undifferentiated goods- and services-producing activities of households for own use.
B559: GDP at constant prices was revised according to the results of the Fifth National Economic Census.
B560: Derived sum of gross domestic saving, net factor income from abroad, and net current transfers from abroad.
B561: Estimated as GDP by expenditure less final consumption plus statistical discrepancy.
B562: Estimated using the annual average exchange rate published by State Administration of Foreign Exchange.
B563: The scope of indicators are from data for industrial enterprises above a designated size (annual revenue from principal business of over CNY20 million).
B564: Original values were indexed in the previous year.
B565: Refers to hydropower, thermal power, nuclear power, wind power, and solar power.
B566: Rate refers to percentage change over previous year. A negative value indicates that the deforestation rate is decreasing (i.e., reforestation).
B567: Gross domestic product in 2015 United States dollars per cubic meter of total freshwater withdrawal.
B568: Disasters may include drought, extreme temperature, flood, landslide, storm, or wildfire.
B571: Refers to household facilities, articles, and services.
B573: For 2001–2015, refers to the PRC's consumer price category "touring and outing". For 2016 onward, refers to the consumer price category "dining out".
B574: For 2001–2015, refers to personal articles and services. For 2016 onward, refers to other supplies and services.
B575: In October 2011, money supply was redefined to include savings of public housing centers and savings of nondepository financial institutions similar to savings of financial institutions.
B576: Refers to broad money aggregate M2.
B577: Refers to deposits excluded from broad money; bonds; paid-in capital; and other items (net).
B578: Bank nonperforming loans to total gross loans are the value of nonperforming loans divided by the total value of the loan portfolio (including nonperforming loans before the deduction of specific loan-loss provisions). The loan amount recorded as nonperforming should be the gross value of the loan as recorded on the balance sheet, not just the amount that is overdue.
B579: Refers to consolidated central and local governments.
B580: For 2000 onward, expenditures of government include all payments on the principal and interest of domestic and foreign debts.
B583: The classifications of revenue and expenditure accounts were adjusted significantly in 2007 and the relative data are not comparable with those for 2000–2006. Expenditure of government adopted a new statistical classification in 2007.
B584: For 2000, 2001 and 2006 onward, total may not add up due to other component not included in the data presentation.
B585: For 2002–2005, expenditures on education include health expenditures.
B586: For 2002–2005, data refer to economic construction.
B587: For 2000–2011, scores refer to perceptions of the degree of corruption as seen by business people and analysts. Scores range from 0 (highly corrupt) to 10 (very clean) and are not comparable over time. From 2012 onward, an updated methodology was used to calculate scores, and these are presented on a scale from 0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean). Due to the differences in methodology, scores prior to 2012 should not be compared with scores for 2012 onward.
B588: Based on Transparency International’s methodology, an economy’s rank indicates its position relative to the Corruption Perceptions Index of other economies of the world; 2025 ranking compare 182 economies.
B589: Data have been compiled in accordance with the IMF's Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual (sixth edition).
B590: For any given year, a negative value for net inflows of foreign direct investment shows that the value of disinvestment by foreign investors was more than the value of capital newly invested in the economy.
B591: Net other official flows refer to official sector transactions with economies on the Development Assistance Committee List of Official Development Assistance Recipients, which do not meet the conditions for eligibility as official development assistance, either because they are not primarily aimed at development or because they have a grant element of less than 25%. The Development Assistance Committee List of Official Development Assistance Recipients is available at http://www.oecd.org/dac/financing-sustainable-development/development-finance-standards/daclist.htm. Net other official flows also include net export credits. Net flow takes into account principal repayments for loans, offsetting entries for forgiven debt, and recoveries made on grants.
B592: Private flows are flows undertaken by firms and individuals residing in the reporting economy.
B593: These flows include official development assistance, other official flows, and changes in the bilateral long-term assets of the private non-monetary and monetary sectors (such as guaranteed export credits, private direct investment, portfolio investment and, to the extent they are not covered in the preceding headings, loans by private banks).
B594: Data refer to international tourist arrivals at frontiers (overnight visitors only, i.e., excluding same-day visitors).
B595: Ranking is based on the sum of 2021–2025 values.
B596: For 2011, 2017, and 2021, purchasing power parity (PPP) figures are based on results from the 2011, 2017 and 2021 benchmark cycles of the International Comparison Program (ICP). For 2010 (and years prior featured in the Key Indicators Database), PPPs are extrapolated from the reference year 2011. For 2012–2016, figures are interpolated from the PPPs of the two ICP reference years, 2011 and 2017. For 2018–2020, figures are interpolated from the PPPs of the two ICP reference years, 2017 and 2021. For 2022–2025, figures are extrapolated from the 2021 ICP PPPs or imputed based on a regression model.
